html:
Roman empress, sister of Caligula, wife of Claudius and mother of Nero. She was one of the most powerful women of the Julio-Claudian dynasty.

She was a daughter of the popular general Germanicus and a great-granddaughter of Augustus. Her brother Caligula exiled her in 39 CE for plotting against him. In 49 CE she married her uncle, the emperor Claudius, and persuaded him to adopt her son Nero, who was older than his own son Britannicus. She was given the title Augusta, and her birthplace on the Rhine was renamed after her as a colony, today's Cologne.

When Claudius died in 54 CE, ancient writers said she poisoned him with mushrooms. Nero, aged sixteen, became emperor, and for a time Agrippina ruled through him; her face appeared on coins beside his. But Nero, backed by Seneca, pushed her aside. In 59 CE he tried to drown her in a collapsing boat. She swam ashore, and he sent soldiers to kill her. Tacitus tells the story in vivid detail.
